content: Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of tetracycline by inducing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised during coadministration. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of theophylline by enhancing its metabolism through the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2. Close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin lowers the levels or effects of tiagabine by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Rifampin significantly reduces the levels of ticagrelor by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of ticagrelor with potent CYP3A inducers like rifampin. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of tobramycin by enhancing its efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases the levels or efficacy of tofacitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Loss of therapeutic response to tofacitinib may occur when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inducers. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of tolvaptan by increasing its efflux through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels of toremifene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, which accelerates its clearance and reduces its steady-state serum concentration. Caution and monitoring are required. Rifampin lowers the levels or effects of tramadol by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism, leading to a decreased area under the curve (AUC) for tramadol and its active metabolite (O-desmethyltramadol). Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces the levels or efficacy of trimethoprim by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of rifampin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Dosage adjustments of P-gp substrates may be required to avoid serious toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of vadadustat by mechanisms involving OAT1/OAT3 inhibition, potentially leading to excessive hemoglobin response or adverse reactions. Close monitoring is essential. Rifampin and valoctocogene roxaparvovec both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity when combined with medications that elevate liver enzymes. Close monitoring and consideration of alternative therapies are recommended. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of valsartan by mechanisms involving hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are advised. Vemurafenib increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter, while rifampin decreases vemurafenib levels by the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of vilazodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider increasing the vilazodone dose up to twofold (not exceeding 80 mg/day) when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers for more than 14 days. Reduce the dose to the original level within 14 days after discontinuing the inducer. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vinblastine and vincristine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal and vinorelbine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing efflux through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases the levels of vortioxetine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider increasing the vortioxetine dose (up to three times the original dose) when coadministered with strong CYP inducers for more than 14 days. Reduce the dose to the original level within 14 days after discontinuing the inducer. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of warfarin by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin reduces the levels of zidovudine by increasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of zolpidem by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifampin reduces acetaminophen levels by increasing its metabolism, potentially enhancing hepatotoxic metabolite formation. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of aliskiren by enhancing its efflux through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of alosetron by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels of ampicillin by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Bentonite reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases bisoprolol levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces caffeine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases celecoxib levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces chloramphenicol levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. The clinical significance is unknown. Clofazimine reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Ethanol reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is more likely with chronic ethanol use. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin increases leflunomide effects by enhancing the metabolism of its active metabolite. The clinical significance is unknown. Levoketoconazole reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces moexipril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces ondansetron levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases opium tincture levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces oxacillin levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases perindopril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces pirmenol levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases ramelteon levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces ramipril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases riluzole levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces sulfamethoxazole levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases thyroid desiccated levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin reduces tibolone levels by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is theoretical, and the clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin decreases trandolapril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Voriconazole reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Rifampin significantly reduces abemaciclib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases abiraterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase abiraterone dosing frequency from once daily to twice daily. Rifampin reduces abrocitinib levels by increasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
